draft.title: Japan closes its borders
card: The Tokugawa shoguns feared that foreign ideas and foreign powers could threaten their rule. In the 1600s they set out to control contact with the outside world.
They banned Christianity, which had been brought to Japan by European traders and missionaries. Japanese people who kept the faith could be punished.
They limited foreign trade to a few ports. Only a small number of Dutch and Chinese traders were allowed, and most Japanese people could not travel abroad.
Japan then had over 200 years of peace and isolation, with little contact with the outside world. The shoguns stayed in control for that whole time.
draft.remember: The Tokugawa shoguns controlled outside contact to protect their rule, which brought peace and isolation.

a.q: Why did the Tokugawa shoguns ban Christianity and limit foreign trade?
opts: They feared foreign influence could threaten their rule
They wanted fewer trading partners than China had
They had lost a war against European traders
They were ordered to by the emperor and court nobles
a.why: The shoguns saw foreign ideas and powers as a danger to their rule, so they controlled contact with the outside world. The emperor did not give these orders, because the shoguns held real power.
a.clue: Think about what the shoguns wanted to protect.

b.q: In the 1700s, a Dutch trader in Japan wants to sell goods to people across the country. What would the Tokugawa rules most likely allow?
opts: Trade only at a few ports, under the shogunate's control
Trade at any port, as long as the trader was not Christian
Trade across the country, if the trader paid the shogun
Trade only with the emperor, who ran all foreign contact
b.why: The Tokugawa shoguns limited foreign trade to a few ports, and Dutch traders were among the few allowed. Being allowed to trade did not mean free movement. The emperor did not run foreign contact.
b.clue: Dutch traders were allowed, but only in certain places.

a.best: They feared foreign influence could threaten their rule

b.best: Trade only at a few ports, under the shogunate's control

problems.detail: The clue 'Dutch traders were allowed, but only in certain places' gives the answer away. It points straight to the only option that limits trade to certain ports.

The card says only Dutch and Chinese traders were allowed. Japan also kept managed contact and trade with Korea (through Tsushima), the Ryukyu Kingdom (through Satsuma) and the Ainu (through Matsumae). The line could say 'mainly Dutch and Chinese traders at Nagasaki' so students are not taught that there was no other contact.
